definition-changed.answer: §2002:4 (4.22) 'One or more boolean operands separated by boolean operators' and §2023:3.23 say the same; 2023's boolean operators also include the shift operators (§2023:8.8.2), a widening only. At 2002 a boolean operand of >>EVALUATE is formed by §2002:7.2.6.1 SR1 of boolean literals and is category boolean by SR11 itself, so the programs the rule governs are unchanged.

pending-clause.answer: The rule assigns categories; §2002:8.8.1.1, 8.8.1.3.1 and 8.8.1.3.6 (arithmetic) change how an arithmetic expression is evaluated, not its category; §2002:8.8.2 (read: 2023's text less shifts) changes no category; §2002:8.8.4.1.1 and 8.8.4.2.4 (relation and abbreviated combined conditions) are format-2 matters, not this format-1 rule. No dependency.

behaviour-switch.answer: The switch is DialectBehavior.CompileTimeArithmeticImplementorDefined (src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Control/DialectBehavior.cs:301), read only by CompileTimeArithmetic.For (src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Frontend/Expressions/CompileTimeArithmetic.cs:44), which picks the mode for operand entry and + - * / inside a compile-time arithmetic expression (§2002:7.2.5.2 GR1; its 34-digit 2002 mode against §2002:8.8.1.3.1.1's 32 digits is the known PB5575-family defect, reaching only results of arithmetic operations). The category of an operand is fixed by its form (§2002:7.2.10.2 SR11: an arithmetic expression is numeric, a boolean expression boolean), not by the mode that evaluates it, so the switch cannot change which programs the rule refuses.
